solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deliberately wicked exercises on Rimbaud's earliest poetry

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: the earliest part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: verse is another word for poetry

explanation.surface: A boy poet's first verses, done as a show of deliberate wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A perverse act is done on purpose to be contrary or wrong, so deliberately wicked is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Private investigator to consider operating illegally

parts.note: to rate something is to consider or judge it

explanation.surface: A detective weighs up whether something is unlawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirate as an adjective describes broadcasting or copying done without a licence, as in pirate radio.

clue.text: It's not supposed to contain a record of annulment

indicators.note: one word contains another by holding it inside

parts.note: something real is actual rather than supposed or imagined
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A supposition about a record being cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeal is the revoking of a law, an annulment of it.

clue.text: Left for dead after exactly what is needed is found in river

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the one before it
one piece is found inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
'that's it' means exactly what is needed

explanation.surface: Someone left for dead finds what they need in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Exited means went out, which is to say left.

clue.text: Juliet had one second to tweet her answer surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Juliet takes a moment to post a surprising reply on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo was Juliet's lover, the beloved person known as a sweetheart.

clue.text: One close to Blunkett's heart taking marijuana as a writing aid

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the heart of a name is its middle two letters

parts.note: pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Something dear to a British politician turns out to involve cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: David Blunkett is a former British Home Secretary; the middle of BLUNKETT is NK, and 'close to' and 'taking' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot of ink was the classic desk accessory for anyone writing with a dip pen.

clue.text: Worthless piece about a Conservative

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: An essay about a Conservative judged to be of no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns GUN into NUG. 'piece' suggests writing but is slang for a firearm; Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means trifling, of no value or effect.

clue.text: An optimist's explanation in support of God

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a gloss is an explanatory note

explanation.surface: A believer's account justifying faith in God.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Pangloss is the relentless optimist in Voltaire's Candide.
explanation.definitionFit: Pangloss is Voltaire's tutor who insists all is for the best, so his name means an incurable optimist.

clue.text: Leave at the end after playwright gets cross

indicators.note: after puts this piece behind the one that follows in the clue

parts.note: Ben Travers was an English writer of farces

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dramatist departs at the finale and gets angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something, to cross it.

clue.text: Went about in twos

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
things arranged in twos have been paired

explanation.surface: People walked round in couples.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is an old formal way of saying to go there.

clue.text: List of items for discussion by a military commander includes death

indicators.note: one word includes another by holding it inside itself

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
end is a synonym for death

explanation.surface: A general's briefing paper has death on the list.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the planned run of topics a meeting will discuss.

clue.text: Distorted representation of a device for carrying around underwear

indicators.note: around tells us one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a tray is a flat board for carrying things
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: A caricature of a tray with a vest draped over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque parody or a distorted imitation of something.

clue.text: Former PM featured in Seattle exhibition

indicators.note: the letters are featured in, that is contained within, the run of words

explanation.surface: A British ex-premier stars in an exhibition in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led the Labour government after the Second World War, so he is a former Prime Minister.

clue.text: Be partly responsible for Conservative statement expressing approbation

parts.note: a tribute is a statement of praise

explanation.surface: A Tory shares the credit with words of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute to an outcome is to help bring it about, playing a part in it.

clue.text: It's easy for the Foreign Office to return girl involved in plots

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it

parts.note: garden plots are beds

indicators.note: returning means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A diplomatic department sends a girl back into some scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plots' suggests conspiracies but means garden beds; 'to return' reverses the department's two letters before the girl joins them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed of roses is an idiom for an easy, comfortable situation, as in 'life is no bed of roses'.

clue.text: Religious fellow not brought up to talk at length

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A clergyman unused to being raised to speak lengthily.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly.

clue.text: The second half of some erotic novel by Swift

indicators.note: the second half of a four-letter word is its last two letters
novel means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Part of a racy book by the author Jonathan Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like the satirist but is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteoric rise is a very rapid one, like a shooting star.

clue.text: Be fond of having knowledge too

parts.note: to like is to be fond of
wise means knowing a lot

explanation.surface: Love a clever person, and the same goes for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise means also or in the same way, a synonym for too.

clue.text: Lee and Maria to develop and improve

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Two people plan to grow and get better.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to make something better, a formal synonym for improve.

clue.text: Appropriate for a toff

parts.note: a swell is old slang for a fashionable, upper-class gentleman

explanation.surface: Fitting attire for a posh gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person. 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: 'You might as well' says an action is suitable, so the phrase works as an adjective of fitness here.

clue.text: Newspaper collecting money for a sailor

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, holding the other piece inside

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A tabloid runs a collection for a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Opening after Bill's arrival

indicators.note: after puts the first piece behind the one that follows

parts.note: an ad is a bill or poster
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A launch that follows Bill turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means a coming or arrival, especially of something important.

clue.text: City centre of Liebnitz occupied by British soldiers

indicators.note: the outer letters are occupied by the inner piece filling them
the centre of an eight-letter word is its middle two letters

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: British troops take over the middle of a German philosopher's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of 'Liebnitz' are B and N; REME goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bremen is a port city in north-west Germany.

clue.text: Extremely fastidious about Irish volunteers needing ID to provide medical assistance

indicators.note: about here means around, one piece circling the other
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy Irish volunteer needs identification before giving emergency help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' and 'to provide' are link words; 'volunteers' uses the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate treatment given to an injured person before professional help arrives.

clue.text: Go to Indiana to retire

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
IN is the postal abbreviation for Indiana

explanation.surface: Head to a US state to spend your retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an idiom for going to bed, which retire also means.

clue.text: Father crossing river on small piece of furniture is certain to succeed

indicators.note: the outer word crosses, or spans, the inner pieces

parts.note: a sire is a father
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: a small piece of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A dad wades over a river perched on a stool, sure to make it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small piece of' takes just the initial of 'furniture'; the river and that letter sit just after the first letter of the father.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sure-fire is guaranteed to work, as in a sure-fire hit.

clue.text: Good to receive one thousand roubles for a pound

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it inside

parts.note: nice is a synonym for good
K is short for a thousand
R is an abbreviation for rouble

explanation.surface: It's nice to get a thousand roubles in exchange for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicker is British slang for one pound sterling.

clue.text: It's best not to shoot one in colour before daybreak

definitions.text: It's best not to shoot one

parts.note: red is a colour
first light is daybreak, so light stands for it

explanation.surface: Advice for a hunter: don't fire at a coloured target before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests a gun, but to shoot a traffic light is to drive through it on red.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a stop signal at a traffic junction is called shooting the lights, which drivers should never do.
